description: Single-conductor copper wire ampacity by AWG and insulation temperature rating. This is the 'automotive practice' standard (project.json rule_config.ampacity_standard = AUTOMOTIVE_PRACTICE): free-air continuous ratings typical of automotive/electronics hookup wire (GXL/SXL/TXL/UL1007/UL1015 style constructions), not a building-wiring code. Chosen over IEC 60364-5-52 / UL 758 because those target fixed mains installations and (a) their published tables don't cover conductors below ~1.5 mm^2 (14 AWG), which is most of a robot control harness, and (b) their grouping/conduit derating factors are calibrated for continuously-loaded raceways in walls, not a flexible loom in open cabinet air -- applying them here would produce confidently-wrong 'too conservative' failures on completely normal 16-24 AWG harness wiring. See P-001 in app/engine/rules/physical.py.
source: Remington Industries 'Copper Hook-Up Wire Ampacity by Insulation Temperature Rating' (Revision 0), a standard-format compilation of single-conductor free-air ampacity used broadly across automotive/electronics wire selection (GPT/GXL/SXL/TXL, UL1007/UL1015, MIL-W-16878/1). Reference ambient 30C (86F).
does_not_cover: Conductors >0000 (4/0) AWG or <40 AWG (out of table range; not expected in a robot harness).

Insulation temperature ratings other than the listed columns (80/90/105/125/150/200 C); a segment whose insulation.temp_rating_c doesn't match a column falls back to the nearest column not exceeding it, or is left unchecked if below 80C.
Conduit-embedded or thermally-insulated-wall installations (this is a free-air table).

Continuous full-rated-current duty over the conductor's full service life at the code-compliance safety margins a building-wiring standard targets; treat P-001 here as a sanity check against thermal damage, not a code-compliance certification.
